nodes.content:
## Why this direction

The node starts as one person's practice. Communion asks that people be known
and stay; Creation asks that we make things for someone real. This Aim points
toward the moment those people are actual members, not an audience.

Different ways people can be part of the community (members, supporters,
collaborators, event-goers) is an open question. It belongs to the first
community Bet as a key unknown, not to this Aim.

## Review notes

Agreed with Tim on 2026-10-20. Review yearly.

properties.direction: Grow from a solo practice into a community of people who are known and make things together.

nodes.title: Community

nodes.content:
## Why this direction

The digital world is where the node's inner life (its Vision, its values, its
plans) becomes visible to people who are not in the room. Embodiment keeps it
honest: the site should point back to real people, real gatherings and real
work, never replace them.

First Light lives under this Aim as a series of Bets. The first is
[[bet-first-light-v1]].

## Review notes

Agreed with Tim on 2026-10-20. Review yearly.

properties.direction: Build a digital world that carries the node's real interiority and points people toward something real.

nodes.title: Digital world

nodes.content:
## The bet

Earlier, First Light was imagined as something built in the dark and revealed
when finished. This system is designed for testable bets, so the first
version is the smallest real thing that can get feedback:

1. The website, with the final draft of the Vision essay.
2. A public view over this planning system (values, aims, outcomes, bets),
   so people can see within it.
3. A way to stay in touch: the email list, written as letters.

The prediction is that the essay plus the system view can generate the
foundational interest the Dec 5 checkpoint describes.

## Which Outcomes it should move

The schema allows one `outcome` per Bet, so this Bet points at
[[outcome-email-list]], the broadest interest signal. At the checkpoint, also
compare results against [[outcome-first-supporters]],
[[outcome-people-who-want-in]] and [[outcome-public-system-view]].
[[outcome-first-gathering]] is not expected to move from the site alone and
needs its own Bet.

## Plan

Confidence is low, so a short Learn step comes first: share the essay draft
and a rough system view with a handful of real people before launch
([[task-first-light-early-readers]]). Then build and launch
([[task-first-light-site]]).

## Guardrail notes

No guardrail risk reported. Two to watch:

- Embodiment: the site should point people toward something real (letters,
  gatherings, conversations), not become the whole relationship.
- No drift: social numbers are watched, not targeted (see
  [[outcome-email-list]]).

## Checkpoints

- 2026-10-20: Bet written. Stage backlog.
- 2026-12-05: Compare observed results with the expectation and set surprise.

properties.expectation: We expect that publishing a website with the final Vision essay and a public view of this planning system will, by 2026-12-05, bring at least 50 email signups, 5 supporters, 2 people who want ongoing involvement, and 5 substantive responses to the system view
key_unknowns: Will the Vision essay resonate with people who don't already know Tim?
Is a view into the planning system interesting to outsiders, or only to us?
Which channels will actually bring people to the site?
What does "being part of it" look like for someone who wants in?

nodes.title: First Light v1: the Vision essay and a public view of the system

nodes.content:
## Why this signal

The email list is the one channel where the node owns the relationship and no
algorithm sits in between. If what goes out reads like letters rather than
marketing, it carries Communion well. Signups measure general interest;
replies are the stronger signal. 50 is a default chosen for a six-week
window. Adjust it if it feels off.

## Watched, not targeted: social metrics

Followers, views and likes are watched for context and can be shown
publicly as proof, but they are not targets. Making for the algorithm is the
exact failure Creation guards against, and a follower target would test
No drift on day one. If one social number is worth noting, prefer the
closest thing to real connection: DMs, replies, people sharing with a friend.

Goodhart check: if followers climb but signups and replies do not, that tells
us something.

properties.check_method: Tim reads subscriber and reply counts from the email tool every Monday and at the Dec 5 checkpoint
properties.signal: Confirmed email list subscribers, plus the number who have replied to at least one letter
properties.target: At least 50 confirmed subscribers by 2026-12-05, with at least 5 who have replied to a letter

nodes.title: Fifty people on the email list

nodes.content:
## Why this signal

Bodies in a room are Embodiment and Communion in one signal. This is the
clearest sign that the digital world is pointing people toward something real.

No Bet covers this yet. The website alone will not produce a gathering; it
needs its own plan.

## Gatherings

(Record each gathering here: date, place, headcount, notes.)

properties.check_method: Tim records date, place and headcount in this node's body after each gathering
properties.signal: In-person gatherings hosted by the node, and the number of people who attended each one
properties.target: At least 1 gathering with at least 10 attendees by 2026-12-05

nodes.title: First in-person gathering with ten people

nodes.content:
## Why this signal

"Demonstrably move matter": interest counts when it pulls money toward the
thing. The first dollar from a stranger is a different kind of signal than
zero. The number is deliberately small; it separates "something is
happening" from "nothing is happening."

## Value check

At review, ask whether supporters are paying for something they genuinely
value, or out of obligation. Support that only comes from pressure would hit
the target and miss the Aim.

properties.check_method: Tim counts payments and pledges from the payment or support platform and direct transfers, every Monday and at the Dec 5 checkpoint
properties.signal: Distinct people (not family or close friends acting as a favor) who have paid for or financially supported something from the node, counted cumulatively from 2026-10-20

nodes.title: Five people support the node by December 5

nodes.content:
## Why this signal

This is the seed of [[aim-community]]: the move from a solo practice to people
who are known and make things together. What "being part of it" means is
still open, and these first conversations are how we learn it.

## People

(Name, date, what they want to do.)

properties.check_method: Tim lists each person and the conversation in this node's body as it happens, and recounts at the Dec 5 checkpoint
properties.signal: Distinct people who have said, unprompted or after a real conversation, that they want an ongoing role in the node (collaborating, joining, helping regularly)
properties.target: At least 2 people by 2026-12-05 (3 would be a strong result)

nodes.title: Two or three people want to be part of it

nodes.content:
## Why this signal

Showing the node's real interiority and plan is the Digital world Aim in
miniature. People should be able to see within the system: what we value,
what we are betting on, and how it is going.

## Value check

Publishing the system should make the node more honest, not more performative.
If the public view starts shaping what we write in it, that is drift.

properties.check_method: Tim confirms the view is live and logs each substantive response in this node's body; recount at the Dec 5 checkpoint
properties.signal: Whether a public view of this planning system is live, and distinct people who respond to it substantively (a message, reply or conversation about its contents, not a like)
properties.target: View live by 2026-12-05, with at least 5 people having engaged with it substantively

nodes.content:
Because we keep talking about beauty: relationships are really one of the most
beautiful things this universe has to offer. Having true commitment, care, and
love is all part of it.

Being _known_ is what separates the real thing from simulated belonging, which
is warm but anonymous. _Staying_ names the cost. Commitment opens us up to real
pain, and that very threat is what makes it meaningful at all.

Communion is also the precondition for an organization that practices the
other two.

## What it rules out

Simulated belonging. Commitment that only lasts while nothing is hard.

## In the body

Showing up in person. Receiving people warmly, and appreciating the time and
memory that form another human.

## From the Vision

"Building relationships in which people are known and committed to each other
... treating these connections like an act of creation itself." See _Vision
2.0_, Incarnation, Crucifixion, and Resurrection.

## Review question

Do we actually know each other, and did we stay when it was hard?

properties.statement: We commit to knowing each other and staying, and treat our relationships as among the most beautiful things we make.

nodes.title: Communion

nodes.content:
We use the tools and capacities given to us to pull more beauty out of them, to
rearrange matter into a more beautiful configuration. Enjoying the beauty of
that process belongs to Contemplation; Creation is the act of making things
more beautiful and giving them away.

It works in concentric circles. First, we are creating for each other within
the org; that is step one. Beyond that, we do want to make things that other
humans can appreciate. But there is still a distinction between making things
for "the algorithm," so to speak, and really imagining it being made for a
real person: maybe someone like yourself, or the members of your org, even if
you don't know them.

## What it rules out

Making for the "blank other." The song for Instagram instead of the song for
the girl you have a crush on.

## In the body

Making with our hands. Pouring our humanity, our unique spirit, into endeavors
that can shine brightly.

## From the Vision

"Giving form to what you discover and offering it to others." See _Vision
2.0_, Creation, Fall, and Incarnation.

## Review question

Who did we actually picture when we made this?

properties.statement: We shape what we've been given into something more beautiful, and offer it to someone real.

nodes.title: Creation

nodes.content:
Everything ultimately starts in the body. The body isn't a fourth aspiration;
it's the medium all three happen through. We attend with our bodies, make with
our hands, and show up in person.

Seraph will have a digital expression that reaches people who cannot be there.
That world should give people a true taste of the org's interiority while also
pushing them to seek out something real to them.

## What it guards against

A life lived mostly through screens. Digital experiences that become the
destination instead of a way back to bodies, rooms, and people.

## For Bets

Flag a Bet when its digital piece substitutes for in-person practice or
gathering, rather than leading people towards it.

properties.statement: The digital never replaces the embodied; it points back to it.

nodes.title: Embodiment
